facts.statement: Linlongopterus was first named and described in 2015 based on a partial skull and mandible.
facts.quote: It is known from a partial skull and mandible first named and described in 2015 by Rodrigues et al..

facts.statement: The genus was described in a 2015 paper by Taissa Rodrigues, Shunxing Jiang, Xin Cheng, Xiaolin Wang, and Alexander Kellner, containing the single species L. jennyae.
facts.quote: The genus Linlongopterus was described and named in a 2015 paper by Taissa Rodrigues, Shunxing Jiang, Xin Cheng, Xiaolin Wang, and Alexander Kellner in Historical Biology, containing the single species L. jennyae.

facts.statement: The fossil was discovered in Jianchang County, Liaoning province, and consisted of two blocks of material that had to be glued together for preparation.
facts.quote: It was discovered in the rocks of the Jiufotang Formation in Jianchang County, Liaoning province, and is split into two blocks of material which needed to be glued back together for preparation.

facts.statement: The generic name means "forest dragon wing" and the specific name honors Elfriede Kellner, nicknamed Jenny.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Chinese "forest" (lin) and "dragon" (long), as well as the Latinised Greek "wing" (pteron), while the specific name honours the late Elfriede Kellner, nicknamed Jenny, a supporter of paleontology and mother of Alexander Kellner.

facts.statement: Linlongopterus was a large flying reptile.
facts.quote: As a pteranodontoid pterosaur, Linlongopterus would have been a large flying reptile.

facts.statement: Its bony eye socket is positioned lower on the skull than in other pteranodontoids.
facts.quote: Most distinctive is orbit, or bony eye socket, which is lower on the skull than other pteranodontoids.

facts.statement: Its teeth were likely adapted for a piscivorous diet, similar to other pteranodontoid pterosaurs.
facts.quote: They were likely adapted to facilitate a piscivorous diet, similar to that of other pteranodontoid pterosaurs.

facts.statement: It is likely placed within Anhangueria, though the lack of jaw crests and uniform tooth size suggests it was not an anhanguerid.
facts.quote: It was therefore concluded a position within Anhangueria was most likely, though the lack of jaw crests and relatively uniform tooth size indicated it was not an anhanguerid.

facts.statement: A 2024 study found Linlongopterus to be a primitive member of Ornithocheiriformes, sharing tooth size variation with Haopterus, which contrasts with earlier placements in Istiodactyliformes.
facts.quote: A 2024 redescription of Haopterus, though noting anatomical similarities between the genus and Linlongopterus, found it to be a primitive member of Ornithocheiriformes, with which it shared variation in its tooth sized, something generally lacking in istiodactyliforms.

facts.statement: The time range for Linlongopterus is estimated from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
